title: Created backend data model and migrations
prompt_summary: User completed the Laravel and Vue setup and asked for the best next implementation step for the Mason time entry take-home project.
ai_response_summary: Recommended starting with the backend foundation before the Vue interface. Designed the required database structure using companies, employees, projects, tasks, time_entries, and pivot tables for company_employee and project_employee. Provided migration definitions, indexes, constraints, and explained the reason for enforcing the one-project-per-employee-per-date business rule in backend validation.
decisions: Started with the backend schema to make the frontend easier to build and validate.
Used company_employee because employees can belong to multiple companies.
Used project_employee because employees are assigned to one or more projects.
Kept tasks company-specific but not project-specific.
Added indexes for company/date, employee/date, and project/date history queries.
Added a unique constraint to prevent duplicate employee/project/task/date entries.
Planned to enforce the rule that an employee can only work on one project per date through backend validation.

title: Added Eloquent model relationships
prompt_summary: User confirmed the migration step was complete and asked to continue building the Mason Laravel + Vue time entry project.
ai_response_summary: Provided Eloquent model implementations for Company, Employee, Project, Task, and TimeEntry. Added fillable fields, casts, appended employee full name accessor, and all required relationships for companies, employees, projects, tasks, and time entries.
decisions: Added belongsToMany relationships for company-employee and project-employee assignments.
Added hasMany relationships from company to projects, tasks, and time entries.
Added belongsTo relationships from time entries to company, employee, project, and task.
Added an employee name accessor to simplify frontend dropdown labels.
Added casts for active flags and time entry date/hour values.

title: Created database seeders with realistic sample data
prompt_summary: User completed the migrations and model relationship steps and asked to move onto seeders.
ai_response_summary: Provided separate Laravel seeders for companies, employees, projects, tasks, and time entries. Seed data included employees belonging to multiple companies, employees assigned to projects, company-specific tasks, and sample time entries that respect the one-project-per-employee-per-date business rule.
decisions: Used separate seeders instead of placing all seed logic in DatabaseSeeder to keep the project organized.
Created three companies to test the global company filter.
Created employees who can belong to one or more companies to exercise the many-to-many company relationship.
Created projects under specific companies and assigned employees to those projects.
Created tasks that are company-specific but not project-specific.
Added sample time entries for the History tab.
Ensured sample time entries allow multiple tasks on the same project/date but do not violate the one-project-per-date employee rule.

title: Added API routes and read controllers
prompt_summary: User confirmed seeders were working and asked to move on to API routes and controllers.
ai_response_summary: Created API routes and controllers for company lists, company-specific dropdown options, and time entry history. Added endpoints for loading companies, employees/projects/tasks by selected company, listing time entries, and a placeholder store endpoint to be replaced with full backend validation.
decisions: Kept API design small and REST-like for the take-home scope.
Used a company options endpoint so the frontend can efficiently load employees, projects, and tasks after a company is selected.
Filtered history rows by optional company_id so the global company dropdown can affect the History tab.
Used eager loading in the time entry index endpoint to avoid N+1 queries.
Deferred store validation to a dedicated request object because business rule validation is central to the project.

title: Added backend validation and bulk time entry creation
prompt_summary: User confirmed API routes and read controllers were complete and asked to move on to validation and bulk creation.
ai_response_summary: Created a StoreTimeEntriesRequest for validating bulk time entry submissions. Added validation for required fields, valid IDs, company-specific relationships, employee project assignments, duplicate rows, and the rule that an employee can only work on one project per date while allowing multiple tasks for the same project/date. Updated the TimeEntryController store method to create entries inside a database transaction and return formatted created rows.
decisions: Used a Form Request to keep validation logic out of the controller.
Validated relationship integrity on the backend instead of relying only on frontend dropdown filtering.
Allowed multiple task rows for the same employee, project, and date.
Blocked entries where the same employee is assigned to different projects on the same date.
Checked the one-project-per-date rule both within the current request and against existing database records.
Used a database transaction so a bulk submission either fully succeeds or fully fails.
Used individual create calls instead of bulk insert for clearer returned models and simpler take-home readability.

title: Built Vue application shell with company filter and tabs
prompt_summary: User completed backend validation and bulk creation, resolved API validation response behavior, and asked to move on to the Vue app shell.
ai_response_summary: Created the initial Vue Composition API frontend structure. Added a top-level TimeEntryApp component, company filter dropdown, New Entries tab, and History tab placeholders. Loaded companies from the Laravel API and wired selected company state into both tabs.
decisions: Kept the Vue frontend as a Blade-mounted Composition API app without Vue Router or Pinia to match the small take-home scope.
Made the global company filter default to All as required.
Passed selected company state into both tabs so the filter can affect New Entries and History behavior.
Loaded companies once from the API at app startup.
Used simple component boundaries to keep the New Entries and History features easier to build next.

title: Built New Entries tab with editable table and backend submission
prompt_summary: User confirmed the Vue app shell was working and asked to move on to the New Entries tab.
ai_response_summary: Replaced the New Entries placeholder with an editable Vue Composition API table. Added company/date/employee/project/task/hours fields, per-company dependent dropdown loading, add row, remove row, duplicate row, total pending hours, POST submission to the Laravel API, success feedback, and row-level backend validation errors.
decisions: Loaded employees, projects, and tasks per selected company using the existing company options API endpoint.
Cached company options in the component to avoid unnecessary repeat API calls.
Kept each row independently editable so the top-level All company filter still allows mixed-company entry.
Allowed new rows to inherit the selected global company or previous row date for faster entry.
Added duplicate row behavior as a bonus faster data entry feature.
Displayed Laravel validation errors at the row and field level using keys like entries.0.project_id.
Submitted entries in bulk to the backend instead of saving row-by-row.
Emitted an entries-created event so the History tab can refresh after successful saves.

title: Built History tab with filtering, search, sorting, and totals
prompt_summary: User confirmed the New Entries tab tests were working after fixing the controller collection loading issue and asked to move on to the History tab.
ai_response_summary: Replaced the History placeholder with a read-only Vue Composition API table that loads time entries from the Laravel API. Added company filtering through the global company dropdown, client-side search, sortable columns, total hours summary, manual refresh, and automatic refresh signaling after new entries are created.
decisions: Loaded history entries from the existing GET /api/time-entries endpoint.
Used the optional company_id query parameter so the global company dropdown filters the History tab.
Added client-side search and sorting as bonus usability improvements without complicating the backend.
Added total hours based on the filtered visible results.
Used a refresh token from the parent component so successful New Entries submissions can trigger History reloads.
Kept the table read-only to satisfy the core requirement before attempting optional edit functionality.

title: Documented project setup and corrected controller issue from testing
prompt_summary: User confirmed the New Entries and History tabs were working and asked to move on to the next step.
ai_response_summary: Added a reviewer-friendly README covering setup instructions, API endpoints, business rules, data model notes, UX decisions, performance considerations, and AI usage. Also documented a previous testing fix where the TimeEntryController attempted to call load on a regular Laravel support collection, which was corrected by capturing created IDs and re-querying the created entries with relationships.
decisions: Added setup instructions using SQLite to make the project easy for reviewers to run.
Documented the core business rule around one project per employee per date.
Explained frontend UX choices such as company filtering, row duplication, and row-level validation.
Documented performance considerations without over-engineering the take-home project.
Included the controller correction in the AI log to show iterative testing and refinement.
